subject.title: [Bug]: sessions_yield subagent wake can compact parent branch at low context usage

question: Should successful-turn auto-compaction be disabled or sanity-guarded when only aggregate billing usage is available, and should `CompactionEntry` gain a closed trigger/cause field?
rationale: The fix changes core compaction policy and persisted transcript attribution, and the safe behavior depends on maintainer intent for providers that silently accept overflow versus providers that only expose aggregate usage.

options.title: Guard aggregate usage and add trigger metadata
options.body: Use `contextUsage` or a sane last-call/total-token snapshot for overflow decisions, skip or clamp impossible aggregate usage, and persist a closed trigger reason on compactions.

options.title: Only add live proof first
options.body: Keep current policy unchanged until a maintainer or QA run reproduces the exact current-main subagent-yield wake path with provider logs.

options.title: Keep aggregate fallback as policy
options.body: Accept possible low-context false positives to preserve silent-overflow recovery and only add diagnostics for attribution.

recommendation.title: Guard aggregate usage and add trigger metadata
recommendation.body: Use `contextUsage` or a sane last-call/total-token snapshot for overflow decisions, skip or clamp impossible aggregate usage, and persist a closed trigger reason on compactions.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses session runtime, usage accounting, and compaction policy, where recent history shows adjacent ownership.
